items.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Delivers Huge Debut as Hollywood Chases Record Year
items.summary: Columbia Pictures’ Spider-Man: Brand New Day is on pace to notch the second-biggest opening weekend in domestic box office history, with the potential to overtake the top movie after final ticket sales are tallied Sunday night.  Spider-Man: Brand New Day surpassed already lofty projections and is projected to rake in $355 million from 4,487 locations in the U.S. and Canada, an average of $79,117 a location, becoming only the second film in domestic box office history to open above $300 million.  It easily leapt over Spider-Man: No Way Home, which opened with $260.1 million at the domestic box office in December 2021, and could still shoot past the all-time highest domestic opening, which was April 2019’s  Walt Disney’s   Avengers: Endgame, selling $357.1 million over its first weekend.

items.title: El Niño Hits the Panama Canal
items.summary: Two of the world’s most important shipping lanes have been gummed-up by the Iran War.  The canal is poised to reduce its capacity because of the onset of El Niño, a weather pattern that can cause severe droughts and other extreme weather events in various parts of the world.  The canal authority has warned clients that the chances of a severe El Niño system had risen to 81% from 25%.
